# Agentic Engineering

Agentic engineering is the emerging discipline of designing, building, evaluating, and operating production agent systems. It combines software engineering rigor with AI-native patterns — distinct from traditional software engineering, ML ops, or research-lab prototyping.

Core concerns:

- Memory architecture (see [[agentic-memory]]{.related})
- Evaluation and observability (see [[harness-engineering]]{.related})
- Identity, provenance, and audit trails
- Tool ecosystems and skill design
- Failure modes and human-in-the-loop patterns
- Cost accounting and budget discipline

The term is associated with [[karpathy-andrej]]{.author}, whose Sequoia Ascent 2026 talk framed "Software 3.0" as the engineering paradigm where LLMs are a programmable medium rather than a wrapped component.

Distinct from traditional engineering disciplines, agentic engineering treats LLM behavior as a first-class design medium — engineering practices like evaluation, observability, and reproducibility have to be reinvented for systems whose behavior is shaped by prompts rather than code. Trusted AI for science and industry depends on these practices maturing.
